Cell 100: dmin list, byte-aligned

The sorted list of dmin(n), the smallest stopping divisor of each Carmichael number n, as VByte gaps. Each n follows from dmin(n) once dmin(n) is factored.

Switches: A on, B off, C off. What the switches mean.

Times

Build, oracle to file
158.0 min on one thread: 158.0 min for the dmin list and 0.09 min for encoding.

Times are on an Intel Core i9-9900K (8 cores, 16 threads), 64 GB RAM, NVMe SSD, Windows 10. Decode times are in memory. The notes under the results table say how each time is measured.

Build

This file is not hosted. Rebuild it from the oracle with:

make fetch-oracle rebuild-100

The target first builds the dmin list (see intermediate files), then runs the encoder:

dlist_from_paths --orc1 data/carmichael-1e24-oracle.orc1 work/d.raw --threads N
list_build vbyte work/d.raw work/c100-dmin-vbyte.vbg

Verify, decode and certify

make verify-100
make fetch-oracle certify-100

Verify first checks the size and SHA-256 of the file. Then the targets run these commands:

# make verify-100
list_decode work/c100-dmin-vbyte.vbg
# make certify-100
list_decode work/c100-dmin-vbyte.vbg --kind d --certify data/carmichael-1e24-oracle.orc1 --threads N
# make decode-100
list_decode work/c100-dmin-vbyte.vbg --emit work/c100.values.raw --kind d --emit-n work/c100.n.raw --threads N

N is the number of threads. The reproduce page explains the folders and the defaults.
